newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba statement on assets due at 1700 GMT - Hesse.
newsitem.headline: Buba statement on assets due at 1700 GMT - Hesse.

text.p: The Bundesbank will issue a statement on the German government's plans to change Bundesbank accounting methods at 1700 GMT on Wednesday, Bundesbank council member Helmut Hesse told Reuters.
Hesse said the central council had unanimously accepted the statement, which had now been passed on to the German finance ministry.
"The central council approved the statement unanimously," Hesse told Reuters at a reception in Frankfurt.
The Bundesbank council held a regular policy meeting on Wednesday with its agenda topped by a plan to revalue its assets.
German Finance Minister Theo Waigel two weeks ago announced his aim of revaluing the central bank's gold and foreign exchange holdings in a bid to raise money for cash-strapped Bonn budgets.
Financial markets will be looking closely at the Bundesbank statement to assess the level of support the central bank is giving to the Bonn plan.
Waigel's scheme has already unsettled some who say the move will pave the way for a weak single European currency.
The revaluation plan is part of proposals by Waigel to shore up Germany's 1997 budget, straining to meet Maastricht criteria for European monetary union (EMU).
Waigel said on Tuesday a special interim Bundesbank balance sheet had been drawn up and that as a result Bonn could receive a payout from such reserve revaluations this year.
